channel.title: Philadelphiensis on Anti-Federalist Library
channel.description: Recent content in Philadelphiensis on Anti-Federalist Library

item.title: Philadelphiensis I
item.description: Condemns Constitution supporters for attempting to suppress press freedom by demanding writers reveal their names, arguing this censorship reveals the tyrannical nature of the proposed government.

item.title: Philadelphiensis II
item.description: Warns that adopting the Constitution will transform Americans from freemen to slaves, threatening religious liberty and creating despotism worse than British tyranny.

item.title: Philadelphiensis III
item.description: Argues the Constitution transforms American independence into tyranny by creating despotic government without protecting basic liberties.

item.title: Philadelphiensis IV
item.description: Warns that the Constitution will destroy America’s national character by creating a weak government dependent on foreign mercenaries and unable to build a navy while oppressing citizens with standing armies.

item.title: Philadelphiensis V
item.description: Denounces Pennsylvania’s convention for rejecting citizen petitions against the Constitution, arguing this arrogance reveals the tyrannical nature of the proposed government and its wealthy supporters.

item.title: Philadelphiensis VI
item.description: Argues that America’s strength depends on freedom, warning that the Constitution will destroy liberty and make the nation weak, contradicting claims it will distress Britain since despotic governments cannot create true national power.

item.title: Philadelphiensis VII
item.description: Contends that neutrality requires naval power for protection, warning that the Constitution’s government will exhaust resources on standing armies to suppress opposition, leaving no funds for the navy America needs.

item.title: Philadelphiensis VIII
item.description: Celebrates press freedom as the “palladium” of all rights, condemning attempts by Constitution supporters to suppress opposition writers through intimidation tactics while warning that patriotic opponents will resist tyranny.

item.title: Philadelphiensis IX
item.description: Warns that the Constitution will establish martial law and transform free citizens into subjects under a military king, condemning the proposed government as a monarchy-aristocracy conspiracy that threatens all liberties.

item.title: Philadelphiensis X
item.description: Denounces the President as a despotic king with unlimited powers, lamenting that conspirators squandered America’s opportunity for pure democracy.

item.title: Philadelphiensis XI
item.description: Accuses federal convention members of fraud and treason for creating a system that punishes Pennsylvania’s fiscal responsibility, warning that the proposed government will impose crushing uniform taxes while stripping away all remnants of liberty through executive tyranny.

item.title: Philadelphiensis XII
item.description: Defends his essays as necessary warnings against tyranny, challenging critics to refute his proof that the President would be an absolute monarch more dangerous than any in history, and calls for another convention to prevent civil war.
